# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling right now** — Have Grace and her lead coach list every single offering members pay for or receive (classes, PT, nutrition consults, challenges, locker access, etc.). You'll likely find inconsistencies or things nobody knows about. This becomes your master list.

• **Price anchor from PT first** — Start with what your 1-on-1 coaching costs. Everything else prices relative to that value/time investment (e.g., small-group coaching = 60% of PT, class pass = 20% of PT per session). This prevents pricing chaos and makes the menu feel intentional.

• **Create two DISTINCT documents immediately** — Internal (for coaches): shows full margins, upsell pathways, what they can offer. External (for members): shows only what they care about (outcome, price, duration, what's included). Use different language — coaches see "acquisition funnel," members see "build strength in 8 weeks for £X."

• **Embed the member menu on your website/WhatsApp TODAY** — Not perfect, done. Grace should screenshot it, add it to her Instagram bio link, send it to every past inquiry who ghosted. You'll get immediate feedback on what confuses people (that's gold).

• **Designate one person as "menu keeper"** — Every time someone asks "do we offer X?" or coaches make up a new package deal, it goes to this person to update. Prevents menu creep.

**INSIGHTS**

• July was an anomaly—215 leads at £2/lead suggests either a broken tracking pixel, audience overlap, or a creative that went viral but attracted low-intent traffic. August corrected hard: 109 leads, £5/lead. You're now at a sustainable operating level, but the 50% drop in lead volume month-on-month is masking the real story: your close rate (22% in August) is *finally* healthy. April–June were lead-gen disasters (0 sales across 127 leads = dead funnel).

• The math works in August because you've fixed either targeting (reaching women genuinely interested in trials, not curiosity-clickers) or creative (showing the offer/gym value, not just aesthetic). Cost-per-sale sits at £23 (£5 lead × 4.6:1 lead-to-sale ratio), and £52 profit per converted trial is thin but positive. The unit economics only hold if close rate stays 20%+.

• Your spend is flat (£435–£544 is noise), but you're getting 1.6× the leads at half the cost-per-lead versus June. This is efficiency, not scale yet.

**ACTIONS**

1. **Audit and lock down July's winning creative and audience.** Pull the exact ad copy, images, and audience definition that delivered July's volume (even if quality was mixed). July's £2 lead likely had *some* winners inside it—find them via Ads Manager breakdowns (by creative, by audience segment, by placement). Test a 60/40 split next month: 60% audience/creative closest to July's performers; 40% new testing. You need to understand *why* July worked before you can scale it cleanly.

2. **Test two targeting tightens in parallel.** Run one campaign narrowed to women aged 25–45, interested in fitness/wellness, within 10 miles of Belfast (location + intent = higher close rate). Run a second as a lookalike of your August converters (the 24 who became paying customers). The second will be smaller but should drop CPL further and maintain 20%+ close. Budget split: 70/30 toward the lookalike
